name: Cain
charge: Bringing of the fruit of the ground when the sacrificial law required a firstling; refusing correction; and murder of his brother Abel
summary: Cain was the firstborn of the house after it was put out of the garden, a tiller of the ground and a man of the field. He knew the sacrifice ordained in the garden and in process of time brought fruit of the ground instead. Corrected, he grew bitter; called to repent, he refused. He talked with his brother as a friend, drew him out to the field and killed him, then lied to God’s face and took no accountability. Cursed from the earth, marked, and made a fugitive and a vagabond, he built a city in the east among the people already on the earth, and his line carried the music and the weapons until the earth was filled with violence.
offenseFull: Cain was born first, a tiller of the ground and a man of the field, and the ground had been cursed in chapter three, so it did not yield easily (Genesis 4:1-3; Genesis 3:17). He knew the Most High required animal sacrifice, because the sacrificial law was ordained when Adam was clothed with skins (Genesis 3:21; Genesis 9:5). In process of time he brought fruit of the ground; the words in process of time say the falling off was gradual, not sudden. The Lord had no respect to it, and Cain was very wroth and his countenance fell (Genesis 4:3-5). What started it was correction. Correction is grievous to the man who leaves the way, and only by pride comes contention; that grievous spirit nourished envy into bitterness, and Cain is the first hater the scriptures record (Proverbs 15:10; Proverbs 13:10).

The Most High called him to repent: if he did well he would be accepted, and if not, sin lay at the door, and the door is his own mind, and the desire of that sin would be toward him and it would rule over him (Genesis 4:7). Cain talked with his brother, playing the friend while Abel, a prophet, urged him to repent, and drew him out to the field where he spent his days, and killed him there (Genesis 4:8). Christ named the line when he told the men who were plotting his death that they were of their father the devil, a murderer from the beginning, who did not abide in the truth, a liar and the father of it: Satan murdered nobody in the beginning, Cain did, and Cain lied (John 8:44). John says the same, that he was of that wicked one, and killed

his brother because his own works were evil and his brother’s righteous (1 John 3:12). Where envying and strife are, there is confusion and every evil work, and confusion is where every evil work hides (James 3:16). Asked where his brother was, he answered with a lie and a taunt and took no accountability at all (Genesis 4:9).
judgmentFull: Abel’s blood cried from the ground. Cain was cursed from the earth, the ground would no longer yield him her strength, and he was made a fugitive and a vagabond: the same low estate spoken to the serpent (Genesis 4:10-12; Genesis 3:14). A fugitive is a man who kills and escapes the sentence; a vagabond wanders from land to land and settles nowhere that belongs to him, and wherever he goes the ground does not answer him. The curse reached the man himself. Adam was formed of the ground, and the ground was cursed for Cain; the mark set upon him changed him, for at the beginning he looked like everybody else, and his own fear that anyone finding him would kill him says both that the earth was already peopled and that he now stood out among them (Genesis 4:14-15). Vengeance sevenfold was threatened against his killer, and the Most High reserved the matter to himself. From the face of God he would be hid: the Most High stopped dealing with him, and the father he had left was the wicked one.

He went out from the presence of the Lord and dwelt in the land of Nod, east of Eden, the same ground where the cherubims and the flaming sword were set; he found a wife among the people already there and built a city, which is not built for three people, and called it after the name of his son, as the wicked call their lands after their own names (Genesis 4:16-17; Psalms 49:11). The older scholars of Assyria identified that city with Unug, which the Akkadians called Uruk and which scripture calls Erech, and Nimrod later built the beginning of his kingdom on the same ground in the land of Shinar (Genesis 10:8-10). His line kept the trades. Jubal fathered all such as handle the harp and the organ, and music in the wrong hands is a weapon; Tubalcain instructed every craftsman in brass and iron, which is the making of arms, and the Most High says he created the smith that blows the coals and created the waster to destroy (Genesis 4:20-22; Isaiah 54:16). Wisdom says the unrighteous man who went away from her in his anger perished in the same fury with which he murdered his brother, and names his cause as the cause for which the earth was drowned (Wisdom of Solomon 10:3-4; Genesis 6:1-2). The way of Cain stands condemned (Jude 1:11), and the same spirit appears again in Esau, the firstborn, the man of the field, who purposed in his heart to kill his brother (Genesis 27:41).

text.text: And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.
And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.
And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.

And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life;
Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.
And surely your blood of your lives will I require; at the hand of every beast will I require it, and at the hand of man; at the hand of every man’s brother will I require the life of man.
And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.
And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:
But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.
Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: and he that hateth reproof shall die.
Only by pride cometh contention: but with the well advised is wisdom.
And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?
If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.
And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.
And the Lord said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?
And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.

Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.
Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.
For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.

And the Lord God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life:
And now art thou cursed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother’s blood from thy hand;
When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength; a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth.
And Cain said unto the Lord, My punishment is greater than I can bear.

Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth; and from thy face shall I be hid; and I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth; and it shall come to pass, that every one that findeth me shall slay me.
And the Lord said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.
And Cain went out from the presence of the Lord, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.
And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.
Their inward thought is, that their houses shall continue for ever, and their dwelling places to all generations; they call their lands after their own names.
And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth.
He was a mighty hunter before the Lord: wherefore it is said, Even as Nimrod the mighty hunter before the Lord.
And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
And Adah bare Jabal: he was the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle.
And his brother’s name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.
And Zillah, she also bare Tubal–cain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal–cain was Naamah.
Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.
But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.
For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood, wisdom again preserved it, and directed the course of the righteous in a piece of wood of small value.
And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,
That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.
Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.
And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.
